1) Multiscale feature learning is a simple and effective way of learning audio features.

(1) multiscale feature learning can improve the quality of learned features, (2) multiscale feature representations are more robust to changes in the sampling rate of the audio signal, and (3) the proposed multiscale feature learning approach is effective and competitive with state-of-the-art feature learning algorithms

multiscale feature learning is a promising direction for MIR feature extraction.
we have shown that simple approaches to feature learning are effective for music audio and that they can be extended to multiscale representations with only a small increase in computational cost.
we show that simple algorithms can be surprisingly effective, and that multiscale approaches can be very competitive in terms of accuracy, while also offering the benefit of interpretability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multiscale representations we propose outperform the state of the art in the automatic tagging task, while they are comparable to the best state of the art for the similarity metric learning task.
